All quoted errors are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.","batch_rationale":"The pending 16 already cover several esters and carbonyls, salicylaldehyde derivatives, indene, and both strong- and weak-eluent conditions. These supplements add three response-segment tests around measured failures, a connected carbonyl comparison including a two-condition new molecule, a focused check of the m177 anomaly, and alcohol comparisons with useful structural and solvent contrasts. The m196 acquisition complements pending m195, while the m177 selections and pending 2/1 row form a common 150-uL protocol series with an existing 5/1 observation. m200 receives two conditions because its measured pure-EA anchor alone cannot distinguish an early rise from a broadly shifted curve. One new alpha-bromo ester tests transfer in another well-connected family. Most other same-molecule loading variants have nearly identical model predictions; spending the batch on those would add less discrimination than these solvent contrasts, except where the m177 anomaly specifically warrants a cross-load check. Quantile widths are uncalibrated single-model outputs, and frequent zero V1 lower quantiles or quantile crossings make width-only ranking unpersuasive. Expected value comes from correcting how structure and conditions jointly determine both endpoints across related rows. Loading differences, measurement variability, and unrecorded experimental details limit mechanistic conclusions, and the batch does not assume that larger retention or broader elution intervals are intrinsically more valuable."}
